summary: At the open: shares slipped; Treasury yields rose; crude oil jumped.

markets.name: S&P 500
markets.description: The S&P 500 tracks large U.S. companies. It opened 0.37% lower after Wednesday's pullback.

context.text: Oil and borrowing costs were both elevated as trading began.

markets.data_source: S&P Dow Jones Indices and Reuters

markets.name: 10-year Treasury yield
markets.description: The 10-year Treasury yield guides longer-term borrowing costs. It moved from 5.28% late Wednesday to 5.35% early Thursday.

context.text: Mortgage and business-loan rates often respond to this benchmark.

markets.data_source: U.S. Treasury and The Associated Press
markets.range: Wednesday late reading 5.28% · Thursday early reading 5.35%

markets.name: Brent crude oil
markets.description: Brent crude is a global oil benchmark. It surged 3.8% to $104.08 a barrel Thursday morning.

context.text: The Associated Press tied the jump to continuing uncertainty over Middle East supply.
context.evidence: Published Oct. 8, 2026; price and direction match the morning report.

markets.data_source: CME Group and The Associated Press
markets.range: Wednesday late reading $100.27 · Thursday early reading $104.08

markets.name: Nasdaq Composite
markets.description: The Nasdaq tracks many tech companies. It opened 0.49% lower.

context.text: Technology shares can be sensitive to higher long-term interest rates.

markets.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
markets.description: The Dow tracks 30 large U.S. companies. It opened about 179 points lower Thursday.

context.text: Its smaller decline than the Nasdaq showed uneven moves across sectors.

markets.data_source: S&P Dow Jones Indices and Reuters

markets.name: Expected volatility
markets.description: The VIX estimates expected S&P 500 swings. It rose 0.77 point to 15.85 Thursday morning.

context.text: A higher reading means traders are pricing wider near-term moves.

calendar.title: Delta Air Lines earnings
calendar.definition: Quarterly report on passenger demand, fares, fuel costs, and profit.
calendar.hot_label: If demand or profit is stronger
calendar.hot: A stronger report can support airlines and signal resilient travel spending.
calendar.cool: A weaker report can expose rising costs or softer travel demand.

calendar.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
calendar.definition: Tracks price changes for goods and services bought by households.
calendar.hot: Higher readings have often led investors to expect higher interest rates.
calendar.cool: Lower readings have often led investors to expect lower interest rates.

calendar.title: Federal Reserve Beige Book
calendar.definition: Regional survey of business activity, hiring, prices, and credit across the United States.
calendar.prior: Eight weeks of regional reports · Federal Reserve
calendar.hot: Persistent price gains can reinforce concern about inflation.
calendar.cool: Slower demand can strengthen the case for less restrictive policy.

calendar.title: Retail sales
calendar.definition: Measures consumer spending at stores, restaurants, and online sellers.
calendar.hot: Stronger sales can signal resilient demand and support company revenue.
calendar.cool: Weaker sales can point to household caution and softer demand.

calendar.title: Producer Price Index (PPI)
calendar.definition: Tracks prices received by domestic producers before goods and services reach consumers.
calendar.hot: Faster increases can raise concern about costs reaching consumer prices.
calendar.cool: Softer readings can reduce concern about inflation moving through supply chains.
